P1.evidence: No setter and no application referenced, so the read-back is N/A. The frame was the rep's usual two-part version: 'I just want to get a good idea where you're at, really build out what it is you want. And then if there's alignment with what we do, we can obviously walk through the coaching. And if not, that's fine as well.' Notably the 'if not, that's fine as well' clause was the one part he actually acted on later. Agreement requested and given ('Alrighty?' / 'Yeah.'), open question ran verbatim.

P2.evidence: Efficient baseline for a thirteen-minute call. Work was established first and explored properly, including the shift pattern and its unpredictability. Weight was asked with a good comparative follow-up: 'How much do you weigh at the moment?' then 'When you were doing the kettlebells before, where were you at then? Just so I'm clear and I've got context.' Results from the previous kettlebell period were probed ('you said you found a lot of success with it? In what way?'), diet was asked directly, and sleep and energy were both asked with a reason attached — 'I've spoken to a lot of people in the medical field, I know sleep can be a bit of an issue' — followed by 'Do you wake up feeling pretty good?'. Missing: age, height, and any question at all about health conditions or injuries, which is a striking omission on a prospect being pointed toward loaded kettlebell work, even a self-guided version. Current training frequency was never established.

P3.evidence: The surface half was the best-executed in the batch. He asked for the end goal and then refused to accept a vague answer, explaining why: 'a lot of people come on and they say I want to get stronger, want to lose weight. For some people stronger means I want to be able to play basketball with my kids, some people it could be I want to be doing 70 pound kettlebell snatches... everything that we do is tailored to the end outcome so I want to be super clear and tangible and specific.' That produced a hard benchmark — 175 lb and a 150 lb bench equivalent. Then the phase stopped dead. The bridge question was never asked, so the call never left the physical layer. He has a wife, a punishing residency and a body he has lost control of, and not one question went to what any of that means to him. Because the deep why was never surfaced, the only articulated need was structure — and $200 buys structure. The disqualification that followed was a direct consequence of stopping at P3c.

P4.evidence: The previous attempt was covered factually — what he did, when, and that it worked — but never diagnosed. The obvious question, why did something that was working stop, was never asked, and the answer the rep assumed (residency) was never confirmed as the real cause. The prospect half-named his own gap ('guidance is my biggest thing because I don't know exactly') and the rep followed up usefully with 'when you said guidance, in what way did you feel like you needed guidance with it? Is that more so like in terms of how to do the things or just accountability?' — but took the answer at face value. Nothing about why he cannot sustain it alone.

P5.evidence: No consequence frame. Not attempted. This is the phase that decided the call: without any cost of inaction established, a 20 lb gain in a demanding year reads as an inconvenience rather than a trajectory, and structure alone is the natural remedy. A resident heading into another year of rotating 12-hour ICU shifts at his heaviest ever is an unusually strong two-year question, and it was never asked.

P6.evidence: No commitment check of any kind. The rep moved from the guidance question straight into disqualification: 'I feel like the better thing for you would be, have you seen Primal University?' He never established whether the prospect believed the coaching could get him there, and never asked the all-in question. He did check his own read twice, which is good practice — 'Am I accurate with that? I just want to make sure' — but that tests the rep's interpretation, not the prospect's commitment.

P11.evidence: No close was attempted on the coaching — the rep withdrew the offer himself. The only transaction moved was a text link to the $200 self-guided product, which has no onboarding, agreement or Trevor call attached to it.

objection_plays.detail: The money constraint was real and was stated plainly — 'the cost would have been an issue with one-on-one coaching. I'm not there yet. In a year, I would be' — but it arrived at 00:11:45, after the rep had already withdrawn the offer and sent the downsell link, so there was nothing to isolate. Recorded as a miss rather than N/A because the constraint existed throughout and the rep never tested it: no isolation, no financial picture, and no payment plan mentioned, despite the same rep structuring instalments live for another prospect earlier the same week. The prospect also handed over a dated re-entry point — twelve months — and nothing was diarised against it.

Script gap — the self-directed prospect whose stated need is structure rather than accountability. The playbook assumes the buyer wants someone in their corner; this one said the opposite twice. There is no scripted path, and the rep improvised honestly and well: he distinguished the products clearly ('Primal University is pretty much Trevor's brain in resources and programs and guides... that's the coaching, working with Trevor one-on-one'), checked his own interpretation before acting on it, and sent the cheaper option with 'Save you some money, too.' The prospect thanked him for it. Marked hit for the improvisation. The script should own this case, because the correct sequence is to run the consequence frame first and only then decide whether self-direction is a real preference or an untested assumption.

notes: Excellent baseline and the sharpest goal-specificity question in the batch, then the call stopped at the surface: no bridge to the deeper why, no consequence frame, no commitment check, and a disqualification at the nine-minute mark. With only 'I want structure' on the table, a $200 product was the logical answer — but the process never tested whether structure was the whole story. Two corrections: run P5 before deciding a prospect does not need coaching, and when a prospect names a date at which he could afford it, book something against that date.
